note: Comparator data for the continental and global position view. Every series carries its own comparability tier, because these indices measure different things and must not be blended into a single ranking.

A.label: Directly comparable
A.detail: The same variable, published by the same body, computed identically for every country in the set.

B.label: Index-aligned estimate
B.detail: Rwanda's position within a published index whose methodology and country set change between editions. Comparable within an edition, not across them.

C.label: Rwanda-specific
C.detail: Indicators with no peer equivalent. Time-series and target tracking only — never a cross-country comparison.

series.name: Africa AI Governance Index (AAIGI)
series.scale: score out of 4, higher is better
series.measures: Capacity to govern AI, scored across strategy and implementation.
series.reading: Rwanda tops the inaugural index and is the only state scoring strongly on both Strategy & Vision and Implementation & Impact. Only Rwanda, Nigeria and Benin reach the 'Established' band; 16 states are 'Developing', 29 'Nascent' and six 'Minimal'. No African sub-region crosses the midpoint of the scale.
series.publisher: Lawyers Hub and Africa AI Policy Lab
series.coverage: All 54 African states, 80 indicators across 8 pillars

series.name: Government AI Readiness Index
series.measures: Readiness to deploy AI, rather than capacity to govern it.
series.reading: Rwanda ranks 75th globally. Oxford Insights revised the methodology for the 2025 edition, so this position cannot be compared with the 2021 score of 35.16 — the platform holds the two editions as separate series.
series.coverage: 195 governments, 69 indicators across 14 dimensions and 6 pillars

series.name: Government AI Readiness Index
series.measures: Government readiness to implement AI in public service delivery.
series.reading: Rwanda scored 35.16 and ranked 112 of 172, tenth in Africa. The neighbours shown are the countries immediately around it in that edition — the band is tightly packed, so small score movements produce large rank movements.

series.name: Measured frontier AI usage
series.scale: index against an expected value of 1.00
series.measures: Observed frontier AI usage relative to the level expected for an economy of that size and working-age population.
series.reading: Rwanda ranks 111 of 121 economies at 0.20x the expected index. This is the sharpest contrast on the platform: first in Africa on the rules, near the bottom of the world on observed use.

oxfordPillars2021.note: Rwanda's pillar scores in the 2021 edition, as reported in the national readiness assessment. The Data and Infrastructure pillar is the weakest and matches the constraint the 2026 review identifies five years later.

verificationNote: Every series on this page was checked against its publisher in September 2026. The AAIGI values are the published top ten plus South Africa; the Oxford Insights 2025 values are the African cluster reported for that edition.

verification.method: Each index was located at its publisher, and Rwanda's value cross-checked against at least two independent reports.
findings: Africa AI Governance Index — confirmed. Published July 2026 by the Africa AI Policy Lab and Lawyers Hub. Rwanda 3.25 of 4. The publisher was previously recorded as unattributed and has been corrected.

Government AI Readiness Index 2025 — confirmed as an Oxford Insights product, 195 countries. Rwanda rank 75, Kenya 65, South Africa 67, Mauritius 71. Previously recorded as an unnamed publisher and has been corrected.
Government AI Readiness Index 2021 — as cited in the 2022 national assessment. Held separately because the 2025 methodology changed.
Anthropic Economic Index — a real published country view; the Rwanda figures are as reported in the 2026 landscape review rather than re-fetched.
